summary: A joint address usually changes the president's approval very little because the audience is mostly supporters.
realLife: A long look at polls found that a president's approval rarely moved after a yearly address, because viewers were mostly the president's own supporters. One year in the 1990s showed a large rise during a strong economy and a scandal, and a rise in 2005 came with the same week's elections abroad.
sources: Gallup (United States), 'President's Support Usually Unaffected by State of Union', January 26, 2010: https://news.gallup.com/poll/125396/president-support-usually-unaffected-state-union.aspx
